items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: Freddie Washington was dancing for Henry Whetsol.

ctx.x: Another thing is an old one, the film, "Symphony in Black," 1934. It was a short -- nine minutes. They put it on television not ago, and it was Duke's band, with Billie Holliday, and the band at that point was Arthur Whetsob Wetzel, Freddie Jenkins, Cootie Williams, Joe Nance and Lawrence Nanton, Brown, Juan Tizol, Barney Bigard, Johnny Hodges, Otto Hardwick, Harry Carney, Fred Guy, Wellman Braud Wilan Grove, Sonny Greer and Duke. And that was the one that Freddie Washington danced in. Remember making that?
The only time I remember Freddie Washington was at the Apollo Theatre, when we were playing the Apollo Theatre, for a Cotton Club show. Freddie Washington was dancing for Henry Whetsol. "Hyparna."
I see. But you don't remember making a film in Hollywood, a short film of nine minutes called "Symphony in Black?"
